title: BIS Certification Schemes — Complete Guide for Manufacturers
summary: A comprehensive guide to Scheme I (ISI Mark Licence), Scheme II (CRS Registration), and Scheme X (Self-Declaration) under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 2016.
body:
The Bureau of Indian Standards Act 2016 establishes three primary certification schemes for products in India.

**Scheme I — ISI Mark Licence**
The most comprehensive certification scheme. A licensed manufacturer may use the ISI Mark on products manufactured at their facility after BIS grants a licence following product testing and factory inspection. The BIS licence number is printed on the product. Annual surveillance audits are conducted. Applicable to all product categories under mandatory QCOs and voluntary standards.

**Scheme II — CRS Registration (Compulsory Registration Order)**
Designed for electronic and IT goods under the Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order (CRO). Products are registered after testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory. Registration is product-specific, not factory-specific. The CRS mark with registration number must appear on the product and packaging.

**Scheme X — Self-Declaration of Conformity (SDoC)**
A manufacturer's self-declaration that their product conforms to a specified Indian Standard. No BIS factory inspection required. The manufacturer is responsible for ensuring conformance. Applicable only to standards explicitly listed for Scheme X by BIS. Carries full legal liability for the manufacturer.

**Key Differences**
- Scheme I: BIS licenced, factory-inspected, ISI mark, annual surveillance
- Scheme II: BIS registered, lab-tested, CRS mark, product-specific
- Scheme X: Self-declared, no BIS inspection, manufacturer liability

For mandatory products under QCOs, only the scheme specified in the QCO notification is acceptable. Consult the BIS website for the current list of mandatory products and applicable scheme.

title: Frequently Asked Questions — QCO Mandatory Compliance
summary: Answers to common questions about mandatory Quality Control Orders, exemption criteria, and penalty provisions under the BIS Act 2016.
body:
**Q: What is a Quality Control Order (QCO)?**
A: A QCO is a government notification issued under Section 16 of the BIS Act 2016 making BIS certification mandatory for specific products. Once a QCO is in effect, no product covered by it may be manufactured, imported, stored, or sold without a valid BIS certification.

**Q: Who issues QCOs?**
A: QCOs are issued by various central government ministries, including DPIIT, MeitY, MNRE, Ministry of Steel, FSSAI, and others, in coordination with BIS.

**Q: Are there exemptions from mandatory QCO requirements?**
A: Yes. Common exemptions include: goods meant for export only, goods imported for R&D or testing purposes (with prior BIS approval), and small-scale manufacturers meeting turnover thresholds as specified in the QCO. Exemptions must be formally applied for with documentary evidence.

**Q: What are the penalties for non-compliance?**
A: Under the BIS Act 2016, offences related to mandatory certification include imprisonment of up to 2 years and/or a fine of at least ₹2 lakh (up to ₹5 lakh for subsequent offences). Market surveillance by BIS can result in product seizure and recall orders.

**Q: How long does BIS certification take?**
A: Scheme I (ISI Mark): typically 45–90 days from application including testing and factory inspection. Scheme II (CRS): typically 30–60 days from application including lab testing and document review. Timeline varies by product category and BIS workload.

**Q: Can an importer obtain BIS certification?**
A: Yes. For Scheme I, an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) or a Foreign Manufacturer Certification Scheme (FMCS) application is required. For Scheme II (CRS), the foreign manufacturer can directly register through the BIS online portal.

title: BIS Circular No. 2025-ETD-14: Revision to IS 1293 Scope
summary: Circular notifying the expanded scope of IS 1293:2019 to include Type 11 and Type 13 socket adaptors for household use.
body:
**Bureau of Indian Standards
Circular No. ETD/2025/14**
Date: June 15, 2025

**Subject: Amendment to scope of IS 1293:2019 — Plugs and Socket-Outlets for Household and Similar Purposes**

This circular is issued to notify all BIS licencees, importers, and industry stakeholders of an amendment to the scope of IS 1293:2019.

**Amendment Details:**
The scope of IS 1293:2019 has been expanded, effective August 1, 2025, to include:
- Type 11 socket adaptors (3-pin to 2-pin conversion adaptors for household use)
- Type 13 socket adaptors (universal travel adaptors with surge protection rated ≤ 10A)

Both new product types must comply with all existing clauses of IS 1293:2019 and additionally meet the new Clause 6.8 requirements on thermal stability during continuous operation.

**Impact on Existing Licencees:**
Existing IS 1293:2019 BIS licencees who manufacture or intend to manufacture Type 11 or Type 13 adaptors must:
1. Apply for licence extension to include the new product types
2. Submit test reports from an NABL-accredited laboratory covering Clause 6.8
3. Update product marking to include the new IS code edition reference

**Compliance Deadline:** All Type 11 and Type 13 adaptors in the market must bear the ISI Mark by December 31, 2025.

title: MeitY CRO Phase VI — New Product Categories Added
summary: Draft gazette notification expanding the Compulsory Registration Order to include smartwatch chargers and wireless charging pads under MeitY's Phase VI.
body:
**Draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. _____(E)**
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

**Subject: Draft Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) (Amendment) Order, Phase VI**

In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 16 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, the Central Government hereby proposes to include the following additional products in the Compulsory Registration Order:

**Proposed New Product Categories:**
1. Wireless Charging Pads for Consumer Electronics (rated output ≤ 15W)
2. Smartwatch and Wearable Device Charging Adapters (rated current ≤ 2A)
3. USB Power Delivery (PD) Chargers with output > 45W

**Proposed Effective Dates:**
- Domestic Manufacturers: 6 months from final notification date
- Importers: 9 months from final notification date

**Applicable Standards:**
- Wireless Charging Pads: IS/IEC 63369 (proposed)
- Smartwatch Chargers: IS 1293:2019 (Type B compliance)
- USB PD Chargers > 45W: IS/IEC 62368-1

**Comments Invited:** Industry comments on this draft may be submitted to MeitY within 30 days of publication in the Official Gazette.

*Note: This is a draft notification. The final notification may differ. Monitor the Official Gazette for the final version.*

title: NABL Laboratory Accreditation — How to Apply and Prepare
summary: Step-by-step guide for testing laboratories seeking NABL accreditation in the Electrotechnical discipline, including documentation requirements and assessment process.
body:
**National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL)**
Guide to Accreditation in the Electrotechnical Discipline

**Overview**
NABL accreditation demonstrates a laboratory's competence to perform specific tests to international standards. BIS requires testing for mandatory product certification (ISI Mark / CRS Registration) to be conducted at NABL-accredited laboratories with the appropriate test scope.

**Step 1: Determine Your Scope**
Define the specific tests and standards for which you seek accreditation. For electrotechnical work (IS 1293, IS 16046, IS 17017 etc.), the relevant NABL discipline is 'Electrotechnical Testing.' Prepare a draft scope document listing each test method with the corresponding IS/IEC standard and clause number.

**Step 2: Meet the Requirements**
Essential prerequisites:
- QMS conforming to ISO/IEC 17025:2017
- Calibrated and traceable test equipment
- Competent technical personnel (qualification + experience records)
- Adequate laboratory space and environmental controls
- Risk assessment and method validation records

**Step 3: Submit Application**
Apply online through the NABL portal (nabl-india.org). Upload:
- Completed application form
- Organizational chart
- List of key personnel with CVs
- Equipment inventory with calibration certificates
- QMS manual and SOPs
- Draft scope of accreditation

**Step 4: Document Review**
NABL appoints a Lead Assessor who reviews submitted documents. Typical timeline: 4–8 weeks. Non-conformances must be addressed before on-site assessment.

**Step 5: On-Site Assessment**
NABL assessment team visits the laboratory for 1–3 days. Assessors witness test demonstrations, review records, and interview technical staff. Any major non-conformances may require a follow-up visit.

**Step 6: Accreditation Grant**
Upon satisfactory assessment, NABL grants accreditation with a specific scope. Accreditation certificate is valid for 2 years with annual surveillance assessments. Accreditation number format: TC-XXXX (testing) or CC-XXXX (calibration).
